findings.title: GrokLocalCache.readSubscriptionTierDisplay is never called in production
findings.evidence: grep -rn readSubscriptionTierDisplay Sources Tests -> only the declaration (line 96) and one test call site (Tests/AiTaskbarCoreTests/GrokCredentialsTests.swift:78) with an explicit at: file argument. No caller inside Sources -- XAIProvider, which reads Grok credentials, never references GrokLocalCache or the subscription-tier string. Cost: a 14-line enum plus doc comment that decodes a nested JSON-in-JSON payload from ~/.grok/settings_cache.json, plus the Paths.defaultGrokSettingsCache() URL it depends on, exercised only by its own unit test.
findings.impact: Dead production surface: it parses a live user cache file format but the output (subscription tier display string) never reaches the UI or XAIProvider snapshot. Removing it changes no user-visible behavior; if it was meant to feed the xAI cards plan label, that wiring is missing (a functional gap, outside this lens).
findings.fix: Delete GrokLocalCache and Paths.defaultGrokSettingsCache() plus their test if the tier display is not wanted, or wire readSubscriptionTierDisplay() into XAIProvider snapshot construction if it was meant to surface the plan name.

test_red_green.name: characterization test before deletion
test_red_green.assert_before: GrokCredentialsTests still calls GrokLocalCache.readSubscriptionTierDisplay(at:) directly and passes
test_red_green.assert_after: test removed with the deleted code; if wired into XAIProvider instead, a new golden test asserts the snapshot plan label reflects subscription_tier_display

findings.cetico_evidence: GrokLocalCache.readSubscriptionTierDisplay (GrokCredentials.swift:95-108) and Paths.defaultGrokSettingsCache (Paths.swift:74) have no Sources caller. The only caller is GrokCredentialsTests.swift:78.

findings.title: Two of AppLog seven Logger categories are declared but never logged to
findings.evidence: grep -rn AppLog.updates Sources -> 0 hits outside the declaration; grep -rn AppLog.scheduler Sources -> 0 hits outside the declaration. The other five categories (keychain 6, pinning 6, config 11, lifecycle 17, cost 2) all have real call sites.
findings.impact: No functional effect, just two Logger instances nobody writes through, so filtering Console.app or log stream by category==updates or scheduler will always be silent, which could mislead someone into thinking those subsystems are quiet by design rather than unwired.
findings.fix: Delete the updates and scheduler static lets, or start using them at the call sites in UpdateChecker.swift and RefreshScheduler.swift that currently either do not log or use a different category.

test_red_green.name: n/a, no test possible for an unused constant

findings.title: DiskCache.payloadAge() has zero callers
findings.evidence: grep -rn payloadAge Sources Tests -> only the declaration at line 73. freshPayloadWithAge(), the very next method, added for the same hot cache-hit path per its N1-NEX-004 comment, duplicates the same stat plus mtime read and is the one actually called.
findings.impact: 7-line public method (stat and mtime diff under the I/O lock) that duplicates logic already inlined in freshPayloadWithAge(). No reader benefit; it reads as a still-supported API but nothing calls it.
findings.fix: Delete payloadAge(). If a caller resurfaces a need for the age alone without the payload, have it call freshPayloadWithAge() and discard the data half instead of maintaining two stat-and-mtime code paths.

findings.title: SettingsViewModel.reloadFromDisk() is never called
findings.evidence: grep -rn reloadFromDisk Sources Tests -> only the declaration at line 55. Its own doc comment says: use after applyChanges lands so the form dirty state correctly resets. No call site in SettingsView.swift or anywhere else invokes it after apply or save.
findings.impact: The doc comment documents a workflow (call after applyChanges to reset the dirty and Save-button state) that does not happen; hasUnsavedChanges may stay stale after a save unless something else resets original. This is a dead-flag-shaped risk (a documented behavior that never fires), bordering on a functional gap rather than pure ceremony, hence MEDIUM rather than LOW.
findings.fix: Either call reloadFromDisk() at the end of the settings-save flow wherever applyChanges is invoked from SettingsView, or delete the method and its comment if original is already kept in sync some other way; verify which with a test on hasUnsavedChanges after a simulated save.

test_red_green.name: hasUnsavedChanges resets after save
test_red_green.assert_before: after calling the save action, viewModel.hasUnsavedChanges is still true (red, proves reloadFromDisk is not wired)
test_red_green.assert_after: after calling the save action, viewModel.hasUnsavedChanges is false

findings.cetico_evidence: reloadFromDisk (SettingsViewModel.swift:55) has 0 callers. Downgraded from MEDIUM: the claimed 'stale dirty state after save' does not happen, because SettingsView.swift:165-172 calls onDone() and closes the overlay on a successful save. Separately, the method's doc comment is false: `original` is a `let` (:27) and reloadFromDisk replaces only draft (:58), so wiring it in as-is would leave hasUnsavedChanges true.

findings.evidence: grep -rn moveVendor( Sources -> only the declaration at line 195; grep -rn onMove Sources and grep -rn onInsert Sources -> no SwiftUI drag-reorder modifier anywhere. moveVendorUp and moveVendorDown (lines 206, 217) are the ones called from VendorSectionView.swift:214,224 and AnalyticsView.swift:408,415.

findings.title: UsageStore.compactAllHistory() is superseded by compactAllHistoryDetached() and never called
findings.evidence: grep -rn compactAllHistory Sources -> declaration (line 290) plus its own doc reference only; grep -rn compactAllHistoryDetached Sources -> declaration (line 299) plus two real call sites in RefreshScheduler.swift:137,141.
